title: Things you have done

fn.en: Talk about what you have and haven’t done in your life.

useful: Yes, I have. / No, I haven’t.

items.q: The word you put in a question about all of your life: “Have you ___ been to Rio?”
Not once in your whole life: “I’ve ___ played an instrument.”
A person who cannot see is ___.
Four hundred records in one room: a big ___.
You win it in a competition: a ___.
Something you want very much but don’t have yet: a ___.

lines: He [has|have|is] given concerts all over the world. 🎤
He [hasn’t|haven’t|didn’t] seen the written music, because he is blind. 🦯
[Have|Has|Did] you ever left the cinema early? 🎬
No, I’ve [never|ever|not never] left the cinema early, but I’ve often wanted to. ⛔
I’ve always [loved|love|loving] music, but I’ve never [played|play|playing] in a band. 🎵

tts: In the present perfect, the stress is on the past participle in positive sentences, and on haven’t or hasn’t in negative sentences.
He’s GIVEN concerts all over the world.
He HASN’T seen the written music.

items.x: I haven’t been to a festival.
She hasn’t played in a band.

sub.en: Look at the sentences. Which two parts make the present perfect — and where do ever and never go?

items.q: He ___ concerts all over the world.
items.why: have / has + the past participle. give → given, see → seen, win → won.
ever and never go between have and the participle.

items.q: “Have you ever left the cinema early?” — “Yes, ___.”
items.why: A short answer never uses the contraction: Yes, I have.

items.q: He ___ the written music, because he is blind.
I came here ___ I was a child.
items.why: RECYCLED: a finished time (“when I was a child”, “in 2019”) takes the Past Simple, not the present perfect.

items.q: I ___ to Rio three years ago for work.

items.cue: Keep the finished time — which tense?

tts: Nobuyuki Tsujii was born blind, but he started playing on a toy piano at the age of just two. He began learning the piano two years later, and he gave his first big concert in Tokyo when he was twelve years old.
He’s in his twenties now, but he has given concerts all over the world, and he has won many prizes and international competitions.
He has written music for film and TV, too. He hasn’t seen the written music of a single piece he plays.

items.s: He started on a toy piano at two.
He gave his first big concert at twenty.
He has given concerts all over the world.
He has read the written music of the pieces he plays.

use: Yes, I have. / No, I haven’t.
tts: Have you ever left the cinema early? — Oh yes! I’ve left in the middle of a lot of films. I don’t want to sit in a cinema watching something really bad — life’s too short.
I’ve never left the cinema early, but I’ve often wanted to. A few months ago I went to see a terrible film. Someone walked out every five minutes. At the end of the film, I was the only person left.

acts.title: Three collections
text: PAVEL: “I’ve always loved music, but I’ve never played an instrument. Since I was a child I’ve had a big music collection — about four hundred records. I go to two or three festivals a year. I haven’t been to a classical concert before, but I’m going to my first one next week.”
AIGUL: “I’ve been to an art gallery exactly once, when I was eleven, and I remember every room. I haven’t been back. I don’t know why.”

MARAT: “I’ve won one prize in my life: second place in a school chess competition in 2004. My mother has kept it on the shelf for twenty years. I’ve never told her that I lost the final on purpose, because the boy who won was crying.”

items.s: Pavel has never played an instrument.
Pavel has a big music collection.
Pavel has been to a classical concert before.
Aigul has been to an art gallery many times.
Marat has told his mother the whole story.

use: Yes, I have. / No, I haven’t.

items.sit: You want to know if your colleague has been to Brazil at any time in her life.
o: Have you ever been to Brazil?
Did you ever been to Brazil?
Have you ever be to Brazil?

items.sit: Someone asks: “Have you ever left the cinema early?” You have, many times.
You have not played an instrument once in your life.
o: I never have played an instrument.
I’ve not never played an instrument.

items.sit: You describe a pianist who has performed in many countries.
o: He’s given concerts all over the world.
He’s gave concerts all over the world.
He have given concerts all over the world.

items.sit: You went to Rio in 2019 — a finished time.
o: I have went to Rio in 2019.

items.sit: Playing in a band is something you have wanted for years.
o: I’ve always wanted to play in a band.
I always wanted play in a band.
I’ve always want to play in a band.

write.q: Write six sentences about your life: three things you have done, two you have never done, and one thing you did at a finished time in the past (watch the tense).
write.model: I’ve been to three music festivals and I’ve seen my favourite band twice. I’ve won one prize — second place in a school competition. I’ve never played an instrument, and I’ve never been to an art gallery in another country. I’ve always wanted to learn the guitar. I went to my first concert in 2015, when I was nineteen.

speak.q: Ask and answer out loud: Have you ever been to a concert? …an art gallery? …a music festival? Then say two things you’ve never done and one thing you did last year.
speak.model: Have you ever been to a concert? — Yes, I have. Have you ever been to an art gallery? — No, I haven’t. I’ve never played an instrument and I’ve never left a film early. Last year I went to a festival in Almaty.
